title: How his name reached 'Mood Indigo' and the ASCAP three-hit rule
summary: His name got onto 'Mood Indigo' after the 28th year when it was reissued; ASCAP required three hits for membership until BMI began buying numbers.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: When was it that you got your name on Mood Indigo so that you started to get royalties?

After the 28th year when they re-issued it. Can you imagine that? And that was the time, you see, when to belong to ASCAP you had to write at least three hits. You see, that's where the mess-up come, because you couldn't belong to ASCAP if you didn't write three hits.
And a hit was defined as selling what? A certain number of copies of sheet music or --

-- recording, sheet music, anything. That's why they -- Remember, at one time that's why the recording companies wasn't doing anything. Then when BMI came in and started buying up anybody's numbers, ASCAP changed, you see, because ASCAP was losing, you see.
That's the whole thing. They get that thing all mixed up together, look out, and the poor little fish that doesn't know anything, he's the sufferer.
I guess it still happens, too.
